doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Notre Dame Intercollegiate Jazz Festival and the trip to Brazil
summary: His Governors State band won five awards at Notre Dame, leading to a Brazil exchange; he mentions director Rory Carter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Eastman, Eastman, yeah. All of these, across the country. And the director of the band was Rory Carter. And I was in this great band. We had a great band. Because we had some of the professional musicians who were working in Chicago in this band. The band was tough. And we won the award for best band. I won two awards for best saxophonist and best soloist. We won — another guy won best composer, and best vocalist I think. So we won five awards. We took nearly all of it. And it was great. And because of that there was this program that the governor of Illinois had sort of an exchange program with the governor of San Paolo, Brazil. So I went to Brazil as a result of that and stayed down there and they sent someone up here.

So that was all during my school, working on for my master’s degree. Rory Carter eventually became the head of Berklee in Boston. He’s not there now, I think he’s back in Chicago now teaching at another place, but I just ran into him here.
